name: Silicon-gate 3708 multiplexer
summary: Fairchild's 3708 multiplexer was the first product made with silicon-gate MOS processing, which made chips faster and denser and became the industry standard.
description: Faggin and Klein brought polysilicon-gate processing to ICs; Faggin redesigned an eight-channel analog multiplexer as the Fairchild 3708.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: Scored as the silicon-gate process it introduced, which made chips faster and denser, became the industry standard and underlay memories and microprocessors.

market.note: The documented product sale or offer establishes market applicability, without establishing first commercial availability of the complete configuration.

evidence.supports: Faggin reports commercial sales of the 3708.

links.statement: Fairchild’s MOS research followed the Atalla–Kahng MOS report; Faggin and Klein later applied a silicon gate to a MOS multiplexer, replacing the metal-gate approach exemplified by the earlier device.
links.scope: Bell Labs MOS presentation and Fairchild MOS research, 1960 onward; silicon-gate 3708 multiplexer, 1968.
links.alternatives: Other MOS developments and suppliers contributed; metal-gate and alternative transistor technologies also remained available.
links.caveats: Moore describes Fairchild’s response to the Bell Labs presentation, not the engineering chain for every transistor in the 3708. The CHM account identifies the later multiplexer; the 1970 Faggin–Klein full text has not been inspected. No direct personal collaboration or exclusive ancestry is inferred.
links.timing: The Bell Labs result and 1960 report preceded Fairchild MOS research; the 3708 product was introduced by 1968.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 60–61, section IV: Kahng and Atalla presentation, Fairchild’s subsequent MOS work
evidence.supports: Fairchild participant Moore explicitly says their MOS research followed the Kahng–Atalla presentation and describes the insulated gate structure.

evidence.locator: Main narrative paragraphs 1–2: Bell Labs silicon gate and Fairchild 3708
evidence.supports: Identifies silicon-gate adaptation of MOS technology and Faggin’s redesign of a p-channel metal-gate multiplexer into the 3708.
